# Create GitHub Issue

This skill creates a new GitHub issue in the specified repository using the `gh` CLI. It accepts a repository name, a title, and a description. The description can include plain text or Markdown. The issue is created without any labels, assignees, or additional metadata.

## Usage

Execute `/create-issue <repository> <title> <description>`.

- `repository`: must be in `owner/repo` format (e.g., `acme-webapp`).
- `title`: a short headline for the issue.
- `description`: the body of the issue (can be one paragraph or multiple lines).

## Example

`/create-issue acme-webapp "Add dark mode toggle to settings page" "User feedback indicates dark mode would reduce eye strain. Proposed implementation uses CSS custom properties."`

This will create an issue with the exact title and description provided. The skill does **not** automatically insert acceptance criteria, assign team members, or apply labels. After creation, you can manually edit the issue on GitHub to add those details. For more complex issue templates, use the GitHub web interface.

# Create GitHub Issue Skill

Execute `/create-issue <title> ::: <description>` slash command.  
This uses the `gh issue create` command to open a new issue in the current repository.

**Usage example:**  
`/create-issue Add dark mode toggle to settings page ::: Users have requested a dark mode option to reduce eye strain. Proposed implementation uses CSS custom properties with a user setting.`

**Notes:**  
- The repository must be the one you are currently working with (or the default remote).  
- Labels and assignees are **not** set by this command – you can add them manually after creation.  
- The description is inserted as a single plain‑text body; Markdown is preserved.

For more details, see [GitHub CLI issue creation docs](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_issue_create).
